To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the responses of LIF neurons to modulations in mean input are low-pass and the cutoff frequency is a supralinear function of the mean firing rate and (b) the response to modulations of input variance are high-pass and the gain at high frequencies is independent of baseline parameters, including the firing rate.

1) the cutoff frequency of LIF responses is not a constant but increases with firing rate; 2) LIF responses to modulations are dominated by low frequencies for very low baseline firing rate and by high frequencies at high firing rates; 3) LIF responses have a strong dependence on baseline parameters; 4) LIF responses are not dominated by oscillatory resonances; and 5) LIF responses can be made insensitive to the baseline firing rate.
the LIF model shows a strong dependence on baseline parameters in its response to modulations of both its mean and variance.
